claim: Given a repository root with task manifests (PROJECT_BRAIN_SAME_IDENTITY_TASK_V1), mission files and prerequisite files, and an arbitrary interleaving of choose / claim / execute operations issued by the durable worker identity and by an intruder identity while manifests, missions and prerequisites are edited underneath it, the supervisor (1) chooses only causally-ready tasks (valid manifest for that identity, every prerequisite present and hash-bound, mission file hash-bound, not terminal), highest priority first and smallest task id on ties; (2) lets exactly one identity hold a task lease - a different identity never claims, resumes or executes a leased task and the lease owner never changes; (3) refuses to claim or execute after the manifest or mission drifted from the bound hashes; (4) checkpoints once before the first runtime launch when the manifest asks for it (exit 75, runtime not launched); (5) maps the runtime exit code to COMPLETE (0) / BLOCKED (3,4,5) / FAILED (other) and never launches the runtime again once a task is COMPLETE or FAILED; (6) keeps an append-only, contiguously numbered event log per task and writes one evidence receipt per checkpoint and per runtime attempt.
scope_limits: NO continuous-OBS context validation: instance roots carry no canonical/CANONICAL_POINTER.json and missions carry no continuous_obs block, so continuous_obs_runtime.validate_context is never exercised (separately measurable)
NO real runtime process: the executor is injected and returns scripted exit codes; the default subprocess executor and the ASTRA launcher are out of scope
NO concurrent-process lock contention: operations are sequential in one process; the inter-process claim lock is not measured
NO lease-expiry semantics: lease_seconds is never exceeded inside an instance
NO guarantee about state files written by anything other than the supervisor itself
self_description: Measurement of a solver on instances generated after the solver was frozen, judged by oracles in separate files. authority NONE: it records what was observed on this carrier and grants no credit; only a referee-signed run on a public runner may be cited.
